assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Recrystallization
items.clue: A technique for purifying a solid.

items.label: Element
items.clue: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

items.label: Solvation
items.clue: The process in which particles of a solute become surrounded by solvent molecules as the solute dissolves.

items.label: Evaporation (as a separation technique)
items.clue: Heating a solution in an open container so that the solvent vaporizes and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.

questions.stem: Which substance is a compound, and for the correct reason?

options.text: Oxygen, since each of its molecules contains two atoms bonded together
Air, since it contains several elements in the same proportions everywhere
Carbon dioxide, since it contains atoms of two elements bonded in a fixed ratio
Salt water, since the salt and the water have combined to form one new substance

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, CO₂, contains carbon and oxygen atoms chemically bonded in a fixed 1:2 ratio, which is what makes a substance a compound.

questions.stem: Hydrogen and oxygen gases are mixed and ignited. They react to form water. Which statement about the water formed is correct?

options.text: Its hydrogen and oxygen can be separated again simply by boiling it
Its hydrogen and oxygen are bonded together in a fixed ratio
Its hydrogen and oxygen each keep their own properties
Its hydrogen and oxygen are in whatever ratio of gases was mixed

questions.explanation: Water is a compound: every H₂O molecule contains hydrogen and oxygen atoms chemically bonded in a 2:1 ratio, so pure water always has the same composition by mass, whatever proportions of the gases were mixed.

questions.stem: A student dissolves sodium chloride in water to make a clear, colourless solution. Which statement about the solution is correct?

options.text: It is a heterogeneous mixture, since the dissolved salt slowly sinks to the bottom
It is a compound, since the salt and water have bonded together in solution
It is a pure substance, since the salt no longer exists once it has dissolved
It is a homogeneous mixture, since its composition is the same throughout the solution

questions.explanation: The Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions spread evenly through the water, each surrounded by water molecules, in a single phase. Every sample has the same composition, which is what homogeneous means; the ratio of salt to water can vary, so it is a mixture.

questions.stem: A mixture of sand and sodium chloride is stirred with hot water and then filtered. Where is the sodium chloride after filtration?

options.text: In the filtrate, as ions surrounded by water molecules
On the filter paper, since solid cannot pass through it
Nowhere, since the salt stopped existing when it dissolved
In the filtrate, as salt that has melted in the hot water

questions.explanation: Sodium chloride dissolves: its Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions separate and are surrounded by water molecules (solvation). These ions are far too small to be held back by filter paper, so they pass into the filtrate. The insoluble sand stays on the paper. Evaporating the filtrate recovers the salt.

questions.stem: A student wants to obtain pure water from aqueous copper(II) sulfate. Which method should be used?

options.text: Evaporation, as the water is collected when it leaves the dish
Filtration, as the dissolved solid is caught by the paper
Electrolysis, as the solute and water are chemically bonded
Distillation, as the water vapour is condensed and collected

questions.explanation: Heating vaporizes the water; the vapour is cooled in a condenser and the pure liquid water collected. Copper(II) sulfate does not vaporize at 100 °C, so it stays in the flask.

questions.stem: A spot of black ink is placed on the baseline of a strip of chromatography paper, and the bottom of the paper is dipped in water. As the water rises, the ink separates into three coloured spots at different heights. What does this show about the ink?

options.text: It is a mixture of several different dyes
It is a mixture of several different elements
It is a compound the paper has separated out
It is a single dye that has reacted with water

questions.explanation: More than one spot shows more than one component. Each dye is carried a different distance up the paper, according to how strongly it is attracted to the paper compared with the water. The dyes were already present and are unchanged.

questions.stem: Impure solid X is dissolved in the minimum volume of hot water, and the hot solution is filtered. When the filtrate is cooled, crystals of X form. Why do crystals of X form when the solution is cooled?

options.text: X freezes, as the solution is cooled below the temperature at which X melts
X is less soluble in cold water than in hot water, so the excess comes out of solution
Dissolved X sinks and collects at the bottom of the flask as the water cools
Water evaporates as it cools, since the solubility of X does not change

questions.explanation: The hot solution is close to saturated. Cold water can dissolve less X, so on cooling the X that the water can no longer hold crystallizes. The small amounts of soluble impurity stay dissolved.

questions.stem: A student wants to recover all of the potassium chloride, as a solid, from a dilute aqueous solution of potassium chloride. Which method should be used?

options.text: Filtration, as the dissolved solid is held back on the paper
Cooling, as the dissolved solid freezes when cold enough
Evaporation, as the water escapes and the solid is left behind
Decanting, as the dissolved solid settles to the bottom on standing

questions.explanation: Heating the solution in an open dish vaporizes the water, which escapes into the air; potassium chloride does not vaporize, so the solid is left in the dish. Evaporation recovers the solute; distillation would be used to collect the water.
